change.title: ao-replay/8714
change.description: feat(artifacts): add HTML and Markdown files to GitHub issues
change.author: Aditi Chauhan

findings.title: Published artifact URL is returned unchecked; "View on GitHub" can silently do nothing
findings.body: The POST uses `--jq .html_url` and returns `result.trim()` as is. If the response has no `html_url`, jq prints `null` and the dialog still shows "Added to GitHub issue". The "View on GitHub" button then calls `aoBridge.app.openExternal(add.data)` with `void` (GitHubIssueArtifactDialog.tsx:74). The main-process handler rejects anything `isAllowedAppExternalURL` refuses (`frontend/src/main/external-open.ts:23-24`), so the click is an unhandled rejection and the button does nothing. Check that the result is an https github.com URL before returning, and throw a visible error otherwise. Also `.catch` the `openExternal` calls at lines 74 and 89. I could not confirm the shape of the artifacts endpoint's response from this repo, which is why this is only "consider".

findings.title: Label wired to GitHubRepoPicker's hard-coded id; raw <label> instead of the ui Label primitive
findings.body: `htmlFor="cloneRepositoryUrl"` works only because `GitHubRepoPicker.tsx:109` hard-codes `id="cloneRepositoryUrl"`. If the picker's id changes, or it is mounted next to `CloneRepositoryDialog`, the label points at the wrong control or two elements share one id. CLAUDE.md asks for new UI built from `components/ui/*` primitives where one fits. `ui/label.tsx` exists and `CloneRepositoryDialog.tsx:376` uses `Label`, but this dialog uses bare `<label>` (lines 77 and 82) with no styling. Use `Label`, and give the picker an `id` prop instead of reusing the clone dialog's id.

findings.title: Non-UTF-8 content surfaces a raw TypeError; read has no size bound
findings.body: `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true }).decode(...)` throws a TypeError, "The encoded data was not valid utf-8", for an `.html`/`.md` file in another encoding. The dialog shows that message verbatim through `add.error.message` (GitHubIssueArtifactDialog.tsx:102). The Copy action handles the same case with the localized `artifacts.notText` (line 234). The whole file is also read with `arrayBuffer()` and sent over IPC and `gh` stdin with no size check, unlike the capped `readArtifactTextResponse` used by `copy`. A very large file only fails after GitHub rejects it. Map the decode error to a translated message, and consider a size cap before reading.

findings.title: Search path, repo filter and error handling are untested
findings.body: The tests cover publishing and the PR-by-number case only. Nothing exercises the `search/issues` branch (lines 33-38), including the `repository_url` filter that stops a `repo:other/x` qualifier in the query from returning issues from another repository. Nothing covers the plain issue-by-number success case, the `gh` failure and stderr mapping, or an invalid `repo` passed to `findArtifactIssues`. Add cases for a mixed-repository search result, a failing `gh` (non-empty and empty stderr), and a number lookup that returns an issue.

findings.title: New IPC handlers trust their argument types
findings.body: The sibling `app:listGitHubRepos` handler coerces its input (`typeof query === "string" ? query : ""`, line 3897). The new handlers pass `repo`, `query` and `input` straight through. A non-string `query` throws a TypeError at `query.trim()`, and a null `input` throws at `input.repository`. `issuePath` and `publishIssueArtifact` do validate `repo`, `name`, `issue` and `body`, so this only affects the error text. Validating the shape at the handler boundary, as the sibling does, would keep it uniform.

contracts.action: Menu item "Add to GitHub issue" opens the dialog and, on confirm, reads the artifact's full content
contracts.equivalent_path: The Copy action in the same component (`copy`, line 228) reads the artifact via `sessionArtifactFileQueryOptions` and `fetchSessionArtifactFile`.
contracts.before_after: Copy goes through `fetchSessionArtifactFile`, which maps cloud 401/403/404 to specific messages, caps text via `readArtifactTextResponse`, and rejects binary content with `artifacts.notText`. The new `readIssueContent` fetches directly, collapses every non-ok status to `files.error.loadArtifact`, has no size cap, and throws a raw TypeError on invalid UTF-8. It returns the whole file, which is intended so the post is not truncated. The item shows only when `!iconOnly && owner && !session.cloud?.shared` and the extension is html, htm, md or markdown.
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog opens from the menu. The mutation error renders in a role=alert paragraph. After success the title and description change and "View on GitHub" appears.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed read rejects the mutation. The error is visible in the dialog and the user can retry. `sharing.current = true` is reset by the menu's `onCloseAutoFocus`, so focus is not returned to the trigger after the dialog closes (same as the share items).

contracts.action: IPC app:findArtifactIssues runs `gh api` to look up an issue by number or search issues
contracts.equivalent_path: app:listGitHubRepos (`frontend/src/main.ts:3861-3897`) also runs `ensureShellEnv()` then `gh` with `daemonEnv()` and a timeout.
contracts.before_after: The sibling swallows errors and returns `[]`. The new call throws, and `stderr` becomes the error message, so a failure is visible. The sibling also coerces `query` to a string. The new path validates `repo` with a regex and forces `--hostname github.com`. It filters search results to the chosen repository via `repository_url`, and drops pull requests.
contracts.visible_effect: Results appear as a list in the dialog. A 404 shows `issueArtifact.unavailable`. Other errors show raw gh stderr.
contracts.failure_mode: A gh rejection, missing `gh`, or timeout rejects the IPC call. `useQuery` has `retry: false`, so the error is shown and the user can edit the query to retry. Nothing persists beyond the dialog.

contracts.action: IPC app:publishIssueArtifact posts the file body to a GitHub issue through `gh api POST`
contracts.equivalent_path: None in the repo posts content to GitHub through `gh`. It follows the `gh` + `daemonEnv()` pattern of app:getGitHubLogin and listGitHubRepos (`frontend/src/main.ts:3791-3820`).
contracts.before_after: Before the call, the main process validates the repo regex, the extension via `issueArtifactType`, `issue` as a safe integer >= 1, and `body` as a string. The dialog posts only after the user picks an issue and clicks the confirm button. The `selected`/`repo` guard sits in the mutationFn. After success it returns `.html_url` trimmed with no check. The handler does not validate the IPC sender; no other handler in main.ts does either (grep for senderFrame found none).
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog switches to an "Added" state with a View on GitHub button. Errors from gh show in the dialog.
contracts.failure_mode: On timeout (30 s) or gh error the call rejects and the dialog shows the error. A timeout can leave the artifact created server-side while the UI reports failure. Retrying could then post a duplicate. An unvalidated result (`null`) makes the View button inert (see finding).

contracts.action: What bounds the wait for each gh-backed call
contracts.equivalent_path: app:listGitHubRepos uses `timeout: 15000` after `await ensureShellEnv()`; getGitHubLogin uses 3 s and 5 s timeouts.
contracts.before_after: Each new IPC call awaits `ensureShellEnv()` (a cached promise, with no timeout visible in the handler) and then runs a single `execFile` with `timeout: 30_000`. There are no sequential gh calls per IPC call, so the worst case is the shell-env wait plus 30 s. The dialog shows "Loading" for search, and for publish a disabled button reading "Adding…" with the close button hidden and `onOpenChange` ignoring close while `add.isPending`. Both are bounded by the 30 s kill. Search is not cancelled when the query changes: each debounced keystroke spawns another `gh` process that runs to completion.
contracts.visible_effect: In the worst case the user waits about 30 s on search or publish. They cannot dismiss the dialog during publish.
contracts.failure_mode: If the first `ensureShellEnv()` login-shell probe hangs, both handlers hang with no limit of their own. The probe's own timeout is in `resolveShellEnv`/`runLoginShell`, which I did not locate.
contracts.open_question: Does the login-shell probe behind `ensureShellEnv()` have its own timeout?

summary: Adds an \"Add to GitHub issue\" action that posts an HTML or Markdown artifact to a GitHub issue through `gh api`. The main-process validation is sound: the repo regex, `--hostname github.com`, the `repository_url` filter, and PR exclusion all hold. The findings are minor: the returned artifact URL is not checked, so the View button can silently do nothing; the dialog uses a raw label tied to the picker's hard-coded id; content read errors are raw and uncapped; and the search path is untested. I also left one contract open: I did not find a timeout on the shared `ensureShellEnv()` wait.
